470: /// This stops trimming a prefix as soon as it sees non-whitespace or a line
471: /// terminator.
472: pub fn trim_ascii_prefix(
473:     line_term: LineTerminator,
474:     slice: &[u8],
475:     range: Match,
476: ) -> Match {
477:     fn is_space(b: u8) -> bool {
478:         match b {
479:             b'\t' | b'\n' | b'\x0B' | b'\x0C' | b'\r' | b' ' => true,
480:             _ => false,
481:         }
482:     }
483: 
484:     let count = slice[range]
485:         .iter()
486:         .take_while(|&&b| -> bool {
487:             is_space(b) && !line_term.as_bytes().contains(&b)
488:         })
489:         .count();
490:     range.with_start(range.start() + count)
491: }
492: 
493: pub fn find_iter_at_in_context<M, F>(
494:     searcher: &Searcher,
495:     matcher: M,
496:     mut bytes: &[u8],
497:     range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
498:     mut matched: F,
499: ) -> io::Result<()>
500: where
501:     M: Matcher,
502:     F: FnMut(Match) -> bool,
503: {
504:     // This strange dance is to account for the possibility of look-ahead in
505:     // the regex. The problem here is that mat.bytes() doesn't include the
506:     // lines beyond the match boundaries in mulit-line mode, which means that
507:     // when we try to rediscover the full set of matches here, the regex may no
508:     // longer match if it required some look-ahead beyond the matching lines.
509:     //
510:     // PCRE2 (and the grep-matcher interfaces) has no way of specifying an end
511:     // bound of the search. So we kludge it and let the regex engine search the
512:     // rest of the buffer... But to avoid things getting too crazy, we cap the
513:     // buffer.
514:     //
515:     // If it weren't for multi-line mode, then none of this would be needed.
516:     // Alternatively, if we refactored the grep interfaces to pass along the
517:     // full set of matches (if available) from the searcher, then that might
518:     // also help here. But that winds up paying an upfront unavoidable cost for
519:     // the case where matches don't need to be counted. So then you'd have to
520:     // introduce a way to pass along matches conditionally, only when needed.
521:     // Yikes.
522:     //
523:     // Maybe the bigger picture thing here is that the searcher should be
524:     // responsible for finding matches when necessary, and the printer
525:     // shouldn't be involved in this business in the first place. Sigh. Live
526:     // and learn. Abstraction boundaries are hard.
527:     let is_multi_line = searcher.multi_line_with_matcher(&matcher);
528:     if is_multi_line {
529:         if bytes[range.end..].len() >= MAX_LOOK_AHEAD {
530:             bytes = &bytes[..range.end + MAX_LOOK_AHEAD];
531:         }
532:     } else {

534:         // Otherwise, it's possible for the regex (via look-around) to observe
535:         // the line terminator and not match because of it.

537:         trim_line_terminator(searcher, bytes, &mut m);
538:         bytes = &bytes[..m.end()];
539:     }
540:     matcher
541:         .find_iter_at(bytes, range.start, |m| {
542:             if m.start() >= range.end {

544:             }
545:             matched(m)
546:         })
547:         .map_err(io::Error::error_message)
548: }

550: /// Given a buf and some bounds, if there is a line terminator at the end of
551: /// the given bounds in buf, then the bounds are trimmed to remove the line
552: /// terminator.
553: pub fn trim_line_terminator(
554:     searcher: &Searcher,
555:     buf: &[u8],
556:     line: &mut Match,
557: ) {
558:     let lineterm = searcher.line_terminator();
559:     if lineterm.is_suffix(&buf[*line]) {
560:         let mut end = line.end() - 1;
561:         if lineterm.is_crlf() && end > 0 && buf.get(end - 1) == Some(&b'\r') {
562:             end -= 1;
563:         }
564:         *line = line.with_end(end);
565:     }
